top_story: The seizure of eight Palestinian homes in Jericho on 6 November, which displaced dozens after armed settler assaults, underscores how settlement expansion is being enforced through direct coercion on the ground rather than only through administrative control. The pressure on Palestinian communities sits alongside exposure of a longer commercial pipeline in which West Bank settlement produce entered Australia labeled as “produce of Israel,” blurring the occupation’s legal boundaries and normalizing its economic gains abroad. On the same day, a leaked UN report alleging that the UAE hired Colombian mercenaries for Sudan’s RSF sharpened scrutiny of Gulf interventionism, linking external patronage to one of the region’s most devastating wars. Together, these developments show how coercion, commercial laundering, and outsourced force are sustaining regional conflicts while pushing civilian dispossession further from public view.
